scope: Package C89 reference and diagnostic one-record slot-106 bridge checked with twelve historical reference vectors plus two named precision cases, all co-executed against pinned original B6F0/B740/B920/B720 x86 callbacks in Unicorn.

101.raw_eax: upper 16 bits of input pointer with the final input WORD replacing low 16 bits via MOV AX

106.raw_eax: full 32-bit post-center Y sum; wrapper returns same EAX

matrix_and_projection_contract.B880_matrix_source: 18 contiguous packed bytes: nine signed WORDs in row-major 3x3 order; target copies four DWORDs plus a final WORD into A8E75C..A8E76D.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B740_matrix: each signed 16-bit matrix/input multiply and each ADD wrap to low 32 bits; row sum uses arithmetic SAR 12, then adds a DWORD translation with low-32-bit wrap and retains sign-extended low WORD as a DWORD camera coordinate.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B740_row_order: cameraX=m[0]*x+m[1]*y+m[2]*z+tx; cameraY=m[3]*x+m[4]*y+m[5]*z+ty; cameraZ=m[6]*x+m[7]*y+m[8]*z+tz, with SAR 12 after each three-product row sum and signed-low-WORD retention before the Z clamp.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B8F0_translation_source: three DWORDs at input+0x14 copied to A8E770/A8E774/A8E778.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B840_translation_alias: The separately measured B840 snapshot writes camera XYZ into A8E770/A8E774/A8E778, aliasing the translation DWORDs read by B740. An extra B840 call therefore mutates inputs for a later transform and is not a passive observation.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B6F0_input: exact WORD reads at +0,+2,+4; values are signed only when B740 MOVSX loads the cells.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B740_camera_z: sign-extended low WORD is stored; values below 1 are overwritten with 1.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B920_reciprocal: focal is a DWORD; SHL 16 wraps to low 32 bits, CDQ/IDIV performs signed division truncating toward zero; B740 clamp makes denominator >=1 on this path.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B920_projection: low-32-bit signed products, arithmetic SAR 16 (rounds negative values down), wrapped DWORD center addition, then low WORD stores at A8E740/A8E746.
matrix_and_projection_contract.B720_output: copies the two projected WORDs unchanged; there is no screen-rectangle clamp in B920/B720.
matrix_and_projection_contract.projection_center_and_focal: B970 copies two 32-bit center arguments; B990 copies one 32-bit focal argument. Neither setter validates or clamps values.
matrix_and_projection_contract.screen_bounds: No fixed width/height bounds are applied by these callbacks. Screen values wrap to 16 bits at B920 and B720 preserves those words. Captured camera Z has already been clamped to at least 1; its pre-clamp value is unavailable after B920 returns.

precision_reprojection_policy.classification: future private render policy illustration; not a native equation or viewport modification
precision_reprojection_policy.formula: private_x = viewport_center_x + effective_focal * camera_x / camera_z; private_y = viewport_center_y + effective_focal * camera_y / camera_z

letterboxed_16_9.policy: vertical-FOV lock to the 360-pixel active viewport, with 60-pixel top/bottom bars

limitations: The captured camera coordinates have already been narrowed to sign-extended low WORDs.
Camera Z has already been clamped to at least 1 before capture; the pre-clamp value is unavailable.
No wider visibility or unclamped camera data is available from this five-field passive snapshot.

falsified_details: B6F0 writes three WORD cells, not three DWORD cells.
B920 stores projected X/Y directly as WORDs at A8E740/A8E746; B720 copies those WORDs unchanged.
supported_details: B740 leaves full sign-extended DWORD camera X/Y/Z after its Z clamp.
The slot-106 wrapper invokes B920 once, reads the five live results after return, and adds no B840/B810 call or game-state write.

proof_boundary: The package reference is a fixed-width C89 behavioral candidate using renderer_contract/hercules_types.h; it is not reconstructed historical source or a FUNCTION_MATCH.
Config and result views are tool-side joined views, not a contiguous original host structure. The diagnostic bridge is one static record and is not a production capture buffer.

The diagnostic bridge is compiled x86 code executed in the same Unicorn address space as pinned original callback bytes; it proves these fourteen synthetic callback paths only (twelve historical reference vectors and two precision cases).

The two precision cases show distinct retained camera X values but the same native screen X WORD. Higher-resolution rational coordinates are a future private rendering policy example, not a native viewport claim.
B840 is excluded because its observed camera snapshot aliases and overwrites the B740 translation inputs; the bridge makes no extra B840/B810 calls.
This does not install a replacement callback into a running game, validate callback-table publication/lifetime/concurrency, or associate captured samples with 3D packets.
No original Windows process, file write to original bytes, assets change, canonical source, recovery state, or Git state is involved.
